title: Phantom Blade Zero True Ending Guide - Every Requirement in Order
description: The complete checklist for Phantom Blade Zero's true ending, Final Battle: every purple Tale, both Crystal Puppet Eyes, all four Acolyte masks, all five Long Pillars, and the order that stops the point of no return from eating your run.
keyword: phantom blade zero true ending, phantom blade zero final battle, phantom blade zero perfect ending, phantom blade zero true ending requirements, phantom blade zero bloodline awakening

facts.label: True ending name
facts.value: Final Battle - also called the Perfect Ending

facts.label: Reward
facts.value: With Heart and Blood (Gold trophy / achievement)

facts.label: Point of no return
facts.value: Leaving the Mirage Estate in Pangzhen for the climb up Mount Soulrend

facts.label: Purple Tales required
facts.value: 9 named Tales, plus Quick Hand Zhang's five fetch requests

facts.label: Pillars required
facts.value: 5 - Weeping Creek Valley, Crimson Forest / Mirrorwood, Meigu Lake midlake, Four Guardians' Mirror, Mirage Estate

facts.label: Key items
facts.value: Both Crystal Puppet Eyes, the Puppet's Tongue, a restored Illusory Pipa

facts.label: Second playthrough
facts.value: Not needed - everything fits in one run, but several steps are missable

sections.title: How the True Ending Actually Triggers
sections.content:
There is no dialogue choice and no hidden morality counter. Beat the regular final boss with the checklist complete and a second fight appears immediately afterwards. Win it and the credits play over the true ending, awarding With Heart and Blood. If the second fight does not appear, one requirement is missing - the game will not tell you which.

That silence is the whole difficulty of this. The checklist spans nine Tales, four boss-gated masks, five pillar trials and two Crystal Puppet Eyes, and any one of them failing quietly reduces you to the Long Roar or Annihilation ending. The order below exists to make the failures impossible rather than to make the run fast.

sections.title: The Deadline: Clear Pangzhen Before You Climb
sections.content:
Every source agrees on the cutoff. Polygon: finish the required Tales before reaching the peak of Mount Soulrend. IGN: complete them before going through the Mirage Estate area in Pangzhen. GamingBolt: the game warns you as you approach the point of no return, and once past it the side content locks into whatever state you left it in.

Everything up to and including the Mirage Estate is therefore your window. In practice that means doing purple Tales when they appear rather than banking them - VGTimes' advice, and the one that prevents most failed runs.

sections.title: The Purple Tales You Need
sections.content:
IGN lists nine Tales as required, all before the Mirage Estate: Whence the Weeping, Deep in the Valley, Pillars of Kunlun, Crimson Manor, Illusion of Inanis, Sha-Chi Powered Boat, Allure of Vanity, Illusory Pipa, and The Herald's Illusion.

Polygon and GamingBolt name three requirements instead of nine - Secrets at the Heart of the Lake, Bloodline Awakening, and all of Quick Hand Zhang's requests - and treat the rest as enabling steps. The two lists are not contradictory so much as different resolutions of the same chain: the nine Tales are what actually unlock the routes, the three are what the game tracks as completion. Treat the nine as the safe answer.

Quick Hand Zhang's fetch requests run across five encounters. Miss one and the chain breaks. Deliver each relic the moment he appears rather than carrying it.

sections.title: Step 1: Four Acolyte Masks
sections.content:
Four optional bosses, each summoned by interacting with a scarecrow, each dropping an elemental mask. The scarecrows are spread across four regions and two of them sit behind story gates.

AcolyteRegionScarecrow locationMask
YanruVillage of LuNorth of the Terrace bell, right side, in the rice fieldBlazing Mask
Lei TingPangzhenUse the Flaming Mane to open the way to Pangzhen Slums; from Old Man Gen's House bell follow the road down toward the lake, scarecrow mid-pathThunder Mask
GuheMeigu LakeMeigu Village East DockVenom Mask
HansuiCrimson ManorInside the manor grounds - save this one for lastFrost Mask

Directions for Yanru, Lei Ting and Guhe are Polygon's. Hansui's region is GamingBolt's, and VGTimes' advice - leave Crimson Manor until last - is the practical one: by then your build can absorb the fight.

Carry resistance accessories before these fights. Every guide that mentions them says the same thing: they turn four awkward boss fights into four normal ones.

sections.title: Step 2: The Four Guardians' Mirror
sections.content:
With all four masks, take the boat from Meigu Lake to the western edge of the region, walk on until you find the mirror, and pass through it. The masks are the key. Inside is a realm holding one of the five Lóng Pillars - and one Crystal Puppet Eye if you are following the route in order (see the next step; sources differ on which eye comes from where, and the page handles that).

Clear the pillar before leaving. Bells do not work inside the Phantom Illusionist Ruins, so the realm is a one-way walk if you skip it. Polygon flags this specifically because it is the step people defer and then lose.

sections.title: Step 3: Both Crystal Puppet Eyes
sections.content:
Two eyes, two locations, and the sources disagree on the mapping. What everyone agrees on is that both are needed and both go into Puppet No. 99.

  • Mountain of Imprisonment - the Yin eye. The region is optional for the story, which is exactly why it gets skipped. VGTimes calls ignoring it one of the standard ways to lose the true ending.
  • Crimson Manor secret boss - the Yang eye, per VGTimes, which describes taking it from the Manor and then sailing to the mirror. Polygon's sequence has both eyes coming from the Manor and the Mountain of Imprisonment without assigning them by name.

The discrepancy is minor and does not change the route: clear both the Mountain of Imprisonment and the Crimson Manor before the point of no return and you have both eyes regardless of which is which.

sections.title: Step 4: The Illusory Pipa and the Three Doors
sections.content:
The Illusory Pipa Tale hands you the pipa itself; restore it, and it becomes the tool that opens the way through the Herald's Illusion. The same Tale chain is what lets you use the three doors there.

Two more gates run off the same hub: the Puppet's Tongue opens the Crimson Manor, and Puppet No. 99 takes both eyes. If the Manor will not open, the Tongue is the item you are missing, not a bug.

sections.title: Step 5: All Five Lóng Pillars
sections.content:
Five pillars, five duels against the Gold-Masked One, and losing any of them means the pillar survives. Polygon lists each pillar with its nearest bell:

RegionNearest bell
Weeping Creek ValleyWeeping Creek Lóng Pillar
Crimson ForestMirrorwood Lóng Pillar
Meigu LakeMidlake Lóng Pillar Dock
Phantom Illusionist RuinsFour Guardians' Mirror (no bell teleport inside)
Pangzhen / Mirage EstateMirage Estate Lóng Pillar

The Mirage Estate pillar is the last one you can reach, so it is also the natural last check before you commit. The Gold-Masked One is the same opponent each time with a bigger toolkit - unblockable throws, sword slashes, kicks - and the answer to the throws is to dodge, not to hold guard.

sections.title: Step 6: The Endgame Boss Chain
sections.content:
With the checklist complete, ring the bell and work up Mount Soulrend. IGN names the closing sequence: Leng Tu, Herald of the Veil, Meng Hua, the Merciful Lady of the Blossom Veil, then Zuo Shang, The True Long, then the extra Final Battle.

Meng Hua is the checkpoint that matters. Beat her with the requirements met and the hidden fight starts; beat her without them and you get the ordinary ending. Zuo Shang - the one-handed Aureate blade is his drop - is the hardest fight in the chain before the true final boss, and the guides that cover him agree on the shape: wear his Sha-Chi down defensively, do not try to out-trade him, and burst only after a guard break or a freeze.

sections.title: Printable Checklist
sections.content:
1. Do every purple Tale as it appears - do not bank them
  2. Deliver each of Quick Hand Zhang's relics in all five encounters
  3. Beat all four Acolytes at their scarecrows (Yanru, Lei Ting, Guhe, Hansui)
  4. Take the four masks through the Meigu Lake mirror
  5. Clear the Lóng Pillar inside the Four Guardians' Mirror realm before leaving
  6. Clear the Mountain of Imprisonment and the Crimson Manor for both Crystal Puppet Eyes
  7. Restore the Illusory Pipa; open the Crimson Manor with the Puppet's Tongue
  8. Insert both eyes into Puppet No. 99
  9. Destroy all five Lóng Pillars, winning all five duels
  10. Clear the Mirage Estate - the last pillar here is the final check
  11. Climb Mount Soulrend and beat Meng Hua, then the hidden boss

Keep a manual save before the Mirage Estate. The game does not offer a warning that distinguishes 'requirements met' from 'requirements failed', and a save from before the cutoff is the only way to recover from a silent miss.

sections.title: Sources and Conflicts
sections.content:
Primary: Polygon's true-ending requirement guide and IGN's All Endings and Requirements, supplemented by GamingBolt (prerequisite list, mask names) and VGTimes (practical ordering, the Yin eye in the Mountain of Imprisonment, the endgame warning). Quest and item names are quoted as those guides print them in English.

Conflicts left standing rather than resolved: the number of required Tales (nine vs three named completions), and which eye comes from which location. Both are recorded above instead of being smoothed over, because a reader who follows either version across the whole checklist still ends up with both eyes and all the Tales.
